source2: Catholic Encyclopedia (1912), 'States of the Church', New Advent - https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/14257a.htm
notes: 1198 marks Innocent III's accession, not a break: papal government continued and was reasserted ('restorer of the States of the Church'). Q4: Roman commune expelled popes, revolt 1143-1155 (Britannica 'Arnold of Brescia').

successor: Mamluk Sultanate expeditionary regime at Zabid (under Ottoman suzerainty from 1517)

1893: Sudanese warlord Rabih conquered Bornu, sacked capital Kuka(wa), made Dikwa his capital. Q4: Sayfawa line ended 1846 amid killings of mais (Britannica 'Kanem-Bornu': dynasty died out); Shehu state continued. European partition came later (1900-02).

Tertry 687: Austrasian mayor Pippin II defeated Neustria, became effective ruler but kept Theuderic III; Merovingian kingship continued to 750/751. Internal shift. Q4: Neustria-Austrasia wars, Childeric II murdered 675, Lucofao 680 (Britannica 'Ebroin').

notes: Sasanians and Turks under Sinjibu crushed the Hephthalites near Bukhara c. 558-561; empire partitioned 560, Sogdiana passed to the Turks. Remnant principalities survived south of the Oxus. Britannica 'Hephthalite' concurs. Q4 unknown.

Capetian kings succeeded father to son 987-1328; 1150 falls inside Louis VII's reign (1137-80), so no break. Q4: Louis VI fought unruly domain barons and Henry I, but no large revolt or civil war recorded.

Franks invaded 773; Pavia (the capital at the end, not Verona/Milan) fell 774, Desiderius captured, Charlemagne became king of the Lombards. Q4: contested succession 756-57 (Ratchis vs Desiderius); Ratchis ousted 749.
